summary: Canonical bootDll boot owner after a bounded numeric-domain cleanup. Existing title resource identifiers are carried into a claimed title catalog header; timing, input, out-view priority, and substick values retain narrow behavior-backed names. The rebuilt boot object is exact for text, rodata, and all 1,069 relocations, its source-owned data is the exact target prefix, and the linked REL is retail-identical.

evidence.summary: The configured GP6E01 object hash, bootDll section extents, and symbol starts establish the target owner boundary and compiler contract. A fresh GC/2.6 build reproduces all 11,684 text bytes, all 208 rodata bytes, and all 1,069 ordered relocations exactly. The 54-byte source data equals the target prefix; the remaining ten target bytes are a zero-filled configured tail gap.

The rebuilt 94,772-byte bootDll.rel is byte-identical to the supplied retail REL. Both files have SHA-1 c2903001e92092befe2c84ebb389d10126f42064 and SHA-256 00236137982857b393649797fc8cd0151f18ea48b5ae833f2244517080af6977.
The claimed title header expresses the existing boot.c DATA_title identifiers through the same-game DATANUM domain without changing their source-level names or values.

The same-owner opening consumer uses BootLightId[0] and BootLightId[1], while same-game pad, object, stream, and camera consumers establish the input-mask, object-priority, and stick-quantization roles used by this owner. The consumer source remains unedited and the complete linked REL is exact. Its standalone source object retains two pre-existing OpeningBgUpdate relocation-ownership differences that resolve identically at link time.
The pinned Mario Party 5 title catalog and boot source support catalog naming and formatting style only. They do not authenticate Mario Party 6 archive indices, sound IDs, or original identifiers.

No GP6E01 title archive or owning catalog table is present in this checkout, so each DATA_title index has not been independently verified against the retail archive. The header entries remain blocked for that catalog-proof step.

The current MP6 msm_se.h does not expose a target-backed symbol for the title confirmation value 1180. TITLE_CONFIRM_SE remains the existing behavior name with a decimal initializer; do not replace it with the MP5 MSM_SE_MENU_40 name or value.

The owner-local lbl_1_bss_4 BSS symbol has no target-backed original name or consumer use; retain the placeholder and do not infer a cross-REL meaning.

The cleanup changes one include/catalog declaration group and one local constant group; no structural ABI/type change or compiler-reconciliation probe was used. Source-quality, public, exact object-relocation, and retail REL gates pass.
